claims: The 8 frozen-model questions (q17-q24) each change one parameter of a metric that q01-q16 already use: a window, an offset, a filter, an aggregation or a threshold. No layer's model defines the variant. With each layer's model left exactly as written for q01-q16, answered through the layer's query-time interface, out of 8: Malloy 8 (8 native), Semantic Rails 6 (6 native), Cube 4 (1 native, 3 workaround), KtX 3 (2 native, 1 precomputed) and MetricFlow 2 (2 native). Each other answer requires a model change, for the reason and the documentation given in shared/frozen_model.yml. Snowflake Semantic Views wasn't assessed: its capture can't be re-run.

Every layer's model was written with q01-q16 in view, so a q01-q16 label says where an answer's logic lives, not whether the layer could answer a question its model wasn't written for; the frozen-model questions test that.

On all 16 questions, the 5 layers checked on the current dataset (Semantic Rails, MetricFlow, Cube, Malloy and KtX) return the independent answer key's normalized outputs, with numbers matching within 1e-6. On the 8 frozen-model questions, all 23 answers the layers executed on the current dataset match it too.

Snowflake Semantic Views was captured on 2026-04-07 on an earlier dataset and has not been re-run, so it is left out of that count. Its capture matches the answer key on 14 questions and differs on: q07, q16.

The answer key is SQL written directly against the shared views, not generated by any layer. An agent wrote it from the question text and the raw data without seeing any layer's models or outputs, and a second agent that didn't write it reviewed it (shared/oracle/SEMANTICS.md).

On this data several questions can't tell a right answer from a common wrong one: delivered time never moves an order into another month, no customer orders at two stores, all sessions are at one store on one day, and customer history covers 4 customers. Matching the answer key there is weak evidence of the intended semantics (shared/oracle/SEMANTICS.md).
Shared questions (q01-q07): 7 of 7 match. Semantic-Rails-targeted questions (q08-q16): 9 of 9 match.

9 of the 16 questions (q08-q16) were chosen to exercise features Semantic Rails ships. The Semantic Rails authors wrote every layer's models, so these questions are a capability showcase, not a ranking, and no layer is claimed to be better than another.

Every support label comes from one executable rubric applied to every layer, Semantic Rails included (shared/rubric.md): unsupported when a layer didn't execute the question, precomputed when its answer reads a rollup column the question declares, workaround when the answer depends on SQL written by hand for this pack, and native otherwise. On the frozen-model questions, requires_model_change comes first, when the layer's query-time interface can't express the question with its model unchanged.

q11 asks for a rollup that the shared data already holds in `lifetime_order_count`; it is labeled precomputed for Semantic Rails, Snowflake Semantic Views and KtX; native for MetricFlow, Cube and Malloy.

q12 asks for a rollup that the shared data already holds in `lifetime_spend_cents`; it is labeled precomputed for Semantic Rails, Snowflake Semantic Views and KtX; native for MetricFlow, Cube and Malloy.

q17 asks for a rollup that the shared data already holds in `converted_order_id` and `converted_at`; it is labeled native for Semantic Rails and Malloy; requires_model_change for MetricFlow, Cube and KtX; not_assessed for Snowflake Semantic Views.

q18 asks for a rollup that the shared data already holds in `converted_order_id` and `converted_at`; it is labeled native for Semantic Rails and Malloy; requires_model_change for MetricFlow, Cube and KtX; not_assessed for Snowflake Semantic Views.

q24 asks for a rollup that the shared data already holds in `lifetime_spend_cents`; it is labeled native for Semantic Rails, MetricFlow, Cube and Malloy; not_assessed for Snowflake Semantic Views; precomputed for KtX.

rules.label: not_assessed
rules.rule: Frozen-model questions only: the layer isn't listed in frozen_model.yml, because this pack can't run it on them.

rules.label: requires_model_change
rules.rule: Frozen-model questions only: the layer's documented query-time interface can't express the question with its model unchanged; frozen_model.yml gives the reason and the documentation.

rules.label: unsupported
rules.rule: The layer didn't execute the question.

rules.label: precomputed
rules.rule: The answer reads a cross-row rollup column that the question declares in bypass_columns, in the executed SQL or in SQL it depends on.

rules.label: workaround
rules.rule: The answer depends on SQL written by hand for this pack: a derived table, a SQL-defined source or cube, or a statement outside the layer's semantic interface.

rules.label: native
rules.rule: None of the above: the layer's semantic constructs only.

layers.label: Snowflake Semantic Views
layers.version: Snowflake CLI + semantic view trial account

rows.title: Orders By Month
rows.business_question: How many orders did we have by month?
rows.expected_semantics: Count distinct orders on the ordered timestamp at month grain.

rows.title: Revenue By Store By Month
rows.business_question: What was revenue by store by month?
rows.expected_semantics: Sum order revenue on ordered time, grouped by store and month.

rows.title: Item Revenue By Product Type By Month
rows.business_question: What was item revenue by product type by month?
rows.expected_semantics: Sum item-grain revenue grouped by product type and ordered month.

rows.title: Average Order Value By Store
rows.business_question: What is average order value by store?
rows.expected_semantics: Revenue divided by orders grouped by store.

rows.title: Orders And Item Revenue In One Query
rows.business_question: Show orders and item revenue in one query by store and month.
rows.expected_semantics: Combine order-grain and item-grain metrics without silently fanning out order counts.

rows.title: New Customer Orders By Month
rows.business_question: How many new customer orders did we have by month?
rows.expected_semantics: Count only first orders, using the ordered timestamp at month grain.

rows.title: Delivered Revenue By Month
rows.business_question: What was delivered revenue by month using delivered time instead of ordered time?
rows.expected_semantics: Sum order revenue anchored to delivered timestamp, not ordered timestamp.

rows.title: Revenue By Historical Customer Segment
rows.business_question: What was revenue by customer segment at the time the order happened?
rows.expected_semantics: Use a temporal-validity relationship from orders to customer history and preserve null when no valid history row exists.

rows.title: Session To Order Conversion Within 7 Days
rows.business_question: What share of sessions converted to an order within 7 days?
rows.expected_semantics: Match sessions to later orders for the same customer within a 7 day window.

rows.title: Orders From Customers With 10 Plus Orders In Month
rows.business_question: What was order volume from customers with more than 10 orders in the same month?
rows.expected_semantics: Use an aggregate-on-aggregate predicate scoped to customer and month, then count qualifying orders.

rows.title: Repeat Customer Orders By Store By Month
rows.business_question: How many repeat customer orders did we have by store by month?
rows.expected_semantics: Count orders from customers whose lifetime order count is greater than one, while preserving outer store and month grouping.

rows.title: Orders By Month With Lifetime Spend Filter
rows.business_question: How many orders did we have by month after applying a query-time filter for customers with lifetime spend of at least 500 USD?
rows.expected_semantics: Apply a query-time customer-scoped predicate over lifetime spend without requiring a separately authored published metric for the filtered result.

rows.title: Daily Orders From Customers With 10 Plus Orders In Month
rows.business_question: What was the daily order volume from customers who placed more than 10 orders in the containing month?
rows.expected_semantics: Evaluate the predicate at customer plus month scope, then return the qualifying orders at day grain.

rows.title: Revenue From Customers With 10 Plus Orders In Same Store Month
rows.business_question: What was revenue by store by month from customers who placed more than 10 orders in that same store-month?
rows.expected_semantics: Evaluate the qualifying predicate at customer plus month plus store scope, then sum qualifying revenue without losing the outer grouping context.

rows.title: Same Store Session To Order Conversion Within 7 Days
rows.business_question: What share of sessions converted to an order at the same store within 7 days?
rows.expected_semantics: Match sessions to later orders for the same customer within a 7 day window and require the store property to match across the event pair.

rows.title: Revenue By Historical Customer Segment As Of Delivered Time
rows.business_question: What was delivered revenue by customer segment as of delivered time?
rows.expected_semantics: Use delivered time as the business clock for the measure and for the temporal-valid join into customer history.

rows.title: Session To Order Conversion Within 14 Days
rows.business_question: What share of sessions converted to an order within 14 days?
rows.expected_semantics: The q09 rule with a 14 day window. A session converted if the same customer placed an order in [session start, session start + 14 x 24 hours).

metricflow: The conversion window is part of the conversion metric's definition (`window: 7 days`). No query option changes it, so a 14-day window needs a new conversion metric.
cube: The model's session-to-order join carries the 7-day window, and a query can't change a join's condition. The SQL API refuses a non-equality join between two Cube queries ("Unsupported expressions in Left JOIN"), and the model exposes no session key to count converted sessions with, since a primary key is hidden unless it is marked public. A different window needs a new join in the model.
ktx: The 7-day window is inside the pack's conversion SQL sources. ktx-sl joins are equality-only, and a semantic query has no join or window option, so a different window needs a new SQL source.

rows.title: Same Store Session To Order Conversion Within 50 Minutes
rows.business_question: What share of sessions converted to an order at the same store within 50 minutes?
rows.expected_semantics: The q15 rule with a 50 minute window. A session converted if the same customer placed an order at the session's store in [session start, session start + 50 minutes).

metricflow: The window and the same-store constant property are part of the conversion metric's definition. No query option changes the window, so a 50-minute window needs a new conversion metric.
cube: The model's session-to-order join carries the 7-day window, and a query can't change a join's condition. The SQL API refuses a non-equality join between two Cube queries ("Unsupported expressions in Left JOIN"), and the model exposes no session key to count converted sessions with, since a primary key is hidden unless it is marked public. A different window needs a new join in the model.
ktx: The 7-day window is inside the pack's conversion SQL sources. ktx-sl joins are equality-only, and a semantic query has no join or window option, so a different window needs a new SQL source.

rows.title: Trailing 3 Month Revenue By Month
rows.business_question: What was revenue over the trailing 3 months, by month?
rows.expected_semantics: For each ordered month, across all stores, sum the revenue of orders placed in that calendar month and the two calendar months before it.

semantic_rails: `rolling` and `prior_period` are query-time expressions, but they run over a dense calendar, and this package declares no calendar entity. The engine refuses the query ("time.fill requires a calendar entity in the package"), so the package needs a calendar entity first.
metricflow: A trailing window is a cumulative metric's `window`, set in its definition. The query interface has no window option, so it needs a new cumulative metric.
cube: SQL API query over a derived table
ktx: ktx-sl rejects window functions in measures, inline query measures included ("Window functions (OVER clause) are not supported in measures"), so a trailing or prior-period value needs a SQL source.

rows.title: Revenue And Prior Month Revenue By Month
rows.business_question: What was revenue by month, beside the revenue of the month before?
rows.expected_semantics: For each ordered month, across all stores, revenue and the revenue of the preceding calendar month, side by side in one row. The first month has no preceding month in the data, so its prior value is null.

semantic_rails: `rolling` and `prior_period` are query-time expressions, but they run over a dense calendar, and this package declares no calendar entity. The engine refuses the query ("time.fill requires a calendar entity in the package"), so the package needs a calendar entity first.
metricflow: A prior-period value is a derived metric with an `offset_window`, set in its definition. The query interface has no offset option, so it needs a new derived metric.
cube: SQL API query over a derived table
ktx: ktx-sl rejects window functions in measures, inline query measures included ("Window functions (OVER clause) are not supported in measures"), so a trailing or prior-period value needs a SQL source.

rows.title: Revenue And Large Order Revenue By Month
rows.business_question: What was revenue by month, and how much of it came from orders of 50 USD or more?
rows.expected_semantics: For each ordered month, across all stores, total revenue beside the revenue of orders whose total is at least 50 USD, in one result.

metricflow: A query's `--where` filters every metric in the query. A metric filter grouped by `order` selects the large orders, so one query returns large-order revenue or total revenue, but not both side by side; that needs a metric with its own `filter:`.
cube: Query filters apply to the whole query, and a filtered measure (`filters:` on a measure) is set in the model. The model exposes no order-total dimension to filter on and no order key for an SQL API query to total revenue per order (a primary key is hidden unless it is marked public), so large-order revenue beside total revenue needs a model change.

rows.title: Average And Largest Item Revenue By Product Type By Month
rows.business_question: What were the average and the largest item revenue per item, by product type by month?
rows.expected_semantics: The q03 grouping, with the average and the maximum of item revenue over item rows instead of the sum.

metricflow: A simple metric's aggregation is part of its definition (`agg: sum` for `item_revenue_usd`). The query interface can't choose another aggregation, so the average and the maximum each need a new simple metric.
cube: A measure's type is set in the model (`sum` for `item_revenue_usd`), and the SQL API refuses an aggregate that doesn't match it. The model exposes no item key and no item-revenue dimension to aggregate per item (a primary key is hidden unless it is marked public), so the average and the maximum need new measures.

rows.title: Orders From Customers With 5 Plus Orders In Month
rows.business_question: What was order volume from customers with more than 5 orders in the same month?
rows.expected_semantics: The q10 rule with the threshold at more than 5 orders in the customer-month instead of more than 10.

cube: SQL API query over a derived table
ktx: The more-than-10 threshold is inside the pack's customer-month SQL source. A query filter is row-level or applies at the query's own grain, so it can't count each customer-month's orders; a new threshold needs a new SQL source.

rows.title: Orders By Month With Lifetime Spend 1000 Filter
rows.business_question: How many orders did we have by month from customers with lifetime spend of at least 1000 USD?
rows.expected_semantics: The q12 rule with the threshold at 1000 USD instead of 500 USD.

summary.scale_up_caveat: Authored-size counts are not yet uniform across layers: the Semantic Rails count omits graph.yml, core_metrics.yml and package.yml. Malloy and Snowflake Semantic Views count their one model file only up to a stretch marker, while the other layers count whole baseline files, including members only the stretch questions use. Do not compare sizes until one script counts every layer's authored files the same way. 'baseline' and 'stretch' here are the 4-model and 7-model sets, not question slices.
